children: Convenience stores and gas stations across the country are increasingly serving up made-to-order pizza that rivals what customers get from traditional pizzerias in a phenomenon that is starting to reshape the competitive map for the industry. A recent pizza-industry research report noted that gas station pizza, long dismissed as low-quality food hardening all day under heat lamps, is improving enough that it's now considered a serious and fast-rising competitor eating into pizzeria profits, especially in small towns without as many dine-in and delivery options.

By installing on-site ovens and kitchens rather than simply selling reheated pizza, the convenience store chain has established a reputation for serving quality pizza and boosted customer loyalty. The pizza business expanded alongside Casey’s

store network through a rural strategy that includes new construction, acquisitions, and investments in kitchens. The company also developed its own distribution network, helping maintain consistent supplies and control logistics costs across locations.

Also in the mix, Hunt Brothers Pizza is a family-owned, Nashville-based pizza business founded in 1991 by four brothers. Rather than operating stand-alone restaurants, the company supplies a branded pizza program to convenience stores and gas stations, particularly in rural communities with limited restaurant options. The chain is now found in more than 11K locations across 33 states. While quality can vary across locations, Hunt Brothers scores very high on consumer review sites in comparison to national pizza chains.
